Dallas Mavericks extend television partnership with FOX Sports
article_text:
The Dallas Mavericks extended their television partnership with FOX Sports in a move aimed at maintaining local broadcast coverage and strengthening the connection between the NBA franchise and its supporters. The agreement reflected the importance of regional sports networks in delivering live basketball, team programming and additional coverage to local audiences.

Mavericks proprietor Mark Cuban said, “FOX Sports has been an amazing partner for the Mavs and our fans. We are excited to do a long-term deal that will allow Mavs fans to stream our games as well as watch on television.”

FOX Sports Southwest Senior Vice President and General Manager Jon Heidtke added, “We are happy to continue our relationship with the Dallas Mavericks, and we look forward to providing Mavs fans with the most complete coverage of their home team for many years to come. We launched our network with the Mavericks, and we look forward to continuing this great partnership.”

The agreement underscored the role of television distribution in extending a team’s commercial reach, supporting advertising inventory and maintaining consistent access to live sporting events. However, the specific financial terms and duration of the extension require confirmation from the original announcement.

Dallas has opened the 2026–27 NBA regular season with two wins and two defeats. The Mavericks lost 128–110 to the Houston Rockets in their season opener before defeating the Indiana Pacers 121–105. A 122–106 loss to the San Antonio Spurs followed, but Dallas returned to winning ways with a 113–109 victory over the Miami Heat on October 26.

As of October 27, Dallas holds a 2–2 record and sits seventh in the Western Conference standings. The team will next host the Oklahoma City Thunder on October 28, followed by a home fixture against Houston on October 30. Both games offer opportunities to build momentum during the opening weeks of the campaign.

The franchise has since moved beyond its former FOX Sports arrangement, adopting a different local broadcast model. Consequently, the historical extension should not be interpreted as a new 2026 agreement. The distinction is important when assessing the Mavericks’ evolving media-rights strategy and its implications for fan access and commercial distribution.

title: World Triathlon partners with Hyrox, recognizing hybrid racing discipline
article_text:
The World Triathlon federation has announced a ‘landmark’ new partnership with the Hyrox series, establishing the mass participation fitness ‘hybrid racing’ concept as a recognized discipline.

This move positions Hyrox as the exclusive official operator of the World, Continental and National Championships for elite hybrid racing, which is now a classified discipline governed by World Triathlon.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Hyrox and World Triathlon will collaborate to create new race concepts, expanding on the three primary categories that World Triaathlon competition will contest Ultimate, Fast, and Ultra.

Going forward, the national federations under World Triathlon will now have the ability to organize national-level races across age groups.

This agreement brings the two bodies together with the aim of eventually receiving Olympic and Paralympic games inclussion.

Speaking on the announcement, World Triathlon president Antonio F. Arimany said: “This agreement is the result of a full year of dedicated work between World Triathlon and Hyrox, and it is enormously gratifying to see it move from negotiation into reality.

“Hybrid Racing is a natural evolution for our movement, and this partnership will not only accelerate the growth of World Triathlon on the global stage, it will open genuine new opportunities for every one of our National Federations to grow participation, engage new audiences, and strengthen our sport at every level. This is exactly the kind of forward-looking collaboration our members deserve.

More than 2 million participants are projected to take part across 105 Hyrox races in over 30 countries during the 2026-27 season.

Earlier this month, the founders of Hyrox furthered their presence in the space, investing in the functional fitness and CrossFit competition series Xenom.

Founded in 2017 in Germany, Hyrox is an indoor fitness competition for both amateurs and professional athletes, which makes mass accessibility one of its primary selling points.

The concept has been steadily growing in popularity over the last few years, having hosted an annual pro/elite championship since 2019, and a top-tier professional circuit, known as the Elite 15, which it has leveraged into sponsorship support from high-profile brands such as Puma, MyProtein, Amazfit, and most recently, Boss Parfums.

Last month, Infront, the Switzerland-based international sports marketing company, sold its majority stake in Hyrox to a consortium led by investment firm L Catterton.

L Catterton was joined in the consortium by Hyrox co-founders Christian Toetzke and Moritz Fürste, as well as digital media and software holding company WndrCo (founded by former DreamWorks chief Jeffrey Katzenberg).

Infront Invested in Hyrox in December 2019, adding the property to its Active Lifestyle division, before acquiring a majority stake in the series in 2022.

title: World Rugby sets out IOC-backed Global Sport for Good programme
article_text:
World Rugby has set out the progress of the Global Sport for Good Initiative, a programme it runs with the International Olympic Committee and three other international federations to strengthen community sport.

Launched in 2024, the initiative brings World Rugby together with FIBA, World Athletics and the Badminton World Federation (BWF). Its aims are to broaden participation and increase sport’s contribution to health and wellbeing, education, inclusion and community development.

The programme has three priorities. The first is training coaches and community practitioners to put participants’ needs at the centre of how sport is delivered. The second is giving unions and regions the tools to measure and evidence the outcomes of their community and education programmes. The third is sharing knowledge between the four federations, their members and wider partners.

So far, the initiative has trained key groups within each federation’s network. These include World Athletics’ Development Commissions, World Rugby’s Regional and Union Training Managers, local facilitators at the FIBA Foundation and BWF’s community educators. More than 500 coaches and educators, and 148 national federations across 122 countries, have taken part.

Each federation has developed its own Theory of Change, linking its work to a set of shared outcomes and indicators. Progress is tracked through a common Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) framework.

For World Rugby, the intended results include building social impact into the strategies and operations of the governing body, its regions and its member unions. They also include increasing the number of inclusive playing opportunities, and recognising coaches and educators as central to delivering social outcomes through the sport.

The initiative forms part of the Olympic Movement’s wider aim of using sport to improve lives.

Jock Peggie, Head of Education, Laws and Compliance at World Rugby, said, “Putting young people at the heart of coaching both in how we deliver, ensuring we are supporting them to play an active role in wider society is a founding principle of rugby union and a key aim of World Rugby.

“I’m proud of how our Regional Training Managers, delivering all around the globe are empowering regions and unions to look closely at the way we bring young people into our sport and help coaches to encourage those young people to lead active lives wherever they grow up.”

title: Newcastle captain Christie extends contract
article_text:
Newcastle Red Bulls captain Tom Christie has extended his contract through to the end of the 2028-29 season.

The 28-year-old New Zealander joined Newcastle from Super Rugby side Crusaders in August 2025.

The flanker has scored six tries in 24 appearances for the Prem side.

"There's no limit as to what can be achieved at this club," he told the club website., external

Head coach Dan McFarland added: "Tom's leadership and professionalism are having a huge influence on our other players, and it's fantastic to get this extension locked in.

"He has an incredibly high level of involvements in our games and his effort level is unsurpassed.

title: England sweat on Fin Smith fitness ahead of Australia clash
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Fin Smith faces a race against time to be fit for England’s autumn opener Australia, but his midfield colleague Benhard Janse van Rensburg will play no part in the campaign.

Head coach Steve Borthwick has revealed Smith will be given until Wednesday to recover from the calf strain sustained on Northampton duty against Leicester on Saturday.

If England’s first-choice fly-half is ruled out, then George Ford or Marcus Smith will be installed as chief conductor for the Wallabies’ visit to Allianz Stadium on November 8.

“Fin has made good progress over the last couple of days and we’re hopeful of his availability against Australia, but that remains unclear at this stage,” Borthwick said.

The outlook on Janse van Rensburg is less positive, with the Bristol centre being stood down from full rugby duties indefinitely.

Van Rensburg has received two significant concussions in his last three games, the most recent of which saw him knocked unconscious when attempting a tackle on England colleague Henry Pollock against Northampton on October 3.

The South African-born centre made his Test debut against Fiji in July but must now wait until the Six Nations to win his third cap after being stood down from the second phase of the Nations Championship next month.

“Benhard has seen a specialist and been advised to take a number of weeks of non-contact work before his reintroduction to rugby over the coming weeks,” Borthwick said.

Flanker Guy Pepper will also miss the Tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, as well as finals weekend, because of the ankle injury he sustained playing for Bath against Gloucester on Friday.

There is better news over Seb Atkinson (knee) and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (hamstring), however, with both players on course to be available for Gloucester and Exeter respectively this weekend.

England’s Leicester and Northampton contingent entered camp on Sunday, just 24 hours after engaging in a giant bust-up at half-time of a stormy East Midlands derby.

Tigers lock Ollie Chessum and Saints number eight Pollock were at the heart of the brawl and Borthwick wants to see the same commitment to the jersey at Twickenham this autumn.

“To be clear, nothing overtly illegal,” Borthwick said. “Do I like seeing intensity, passion, pride? Yes. Do I want the players to bring that passion and pride in an England shirt? Absolutely.

“These are young players who have grown up at their clubs and emerged as big players at their clubs. I want that in an England shirt.

“What I think is very good is that the players compete in the way they do one day and then they can come in and be great mates the next day. Ollie and Henry are great mates.

“I actually think it’s a real strength of the game to be able to compete like that in that kind of full-blooded encounter, as heated as that is, and then they’re perfectly fine.”

Borthwick has told his players this autumn will be instrumental in selection for next year’s World Cup.

“We’ve got 12 Tests now until the World Cup,” he said. “There are 10 Tests until I name our 33-man squad.

“This series of games is the last opportunity we have playing southern hemisphere opposition before then.

“I’m looking forward to seeing players compete and perform against this calibre of opposition.”

title: Benhard Janse van Rensburg stood down from rugby as England sweat over Fin Smith injury
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The Bristol Bears and England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg has been ruled out of the Nations Championship Tests in November and faces a period out of the game as he recovers from two concussions in his last three games.

Janse van Rensburg was knocked out playing for Bristol against Northampton in the Gallagher Prem earlier this month having had his second international cap similarly curtailed by a head injury against Argentina in July.

Steve Borthwick, the England head coach, has confirmed that the centre will not feature in games against Australia, Japan and New Zealand over the next few weeks, though he is “hopeful” that Fin Smith will be fit for the opening clash with the Wallabies.

Northampton fly half Smith has not trained this week with a calf injury and faces a race to be fit for next Sunday’s game. The Bath flanker Guy Pepper will miss November, though, with an ankle problem that does not require surgery, and club colleague Kepu Tuipulotu requires further assessment on a bang to the leg in training.

The standing down of Janse van Rensburg comes as a blow to a player handed his debut against Fiji during the first leg of the Nations Championship having becoming eligible after a five-year residency period in England.

In better midfield news for Borthwick, Seb Atkinson is likely to feature for Gloucester this weekend, while Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is may also play for Exeter in this round of Prem fixtures.

Of Janse van Rensburg, Borthwick explained: “He’s had a specialist's opinion and has been advised to take a number of weeks of non-contact work before reintroduction to rugby over the coming weeks.”

Smith has been unable to train having played much of Northampton’s derby defeat to Leicester carrying the calf issue. He will be given as long as possible to prove his fitness, though Borthwick has confidence in his alternative fly half options.

“He's made positive progress these past couple of days. Typically, I would name the team for the Sunday game on around the Wednesday, so that would still be my aim, to try and name the team around that point in time, but I'll be assessing that right at the start of the week.

“But all the news we've got so far is very positive and if Fin’s not available for selection, we have some quality fly halves in George Ford and Marcus Smith available also. So, we're in a positive position now.”

Borthwick’s squad will reassemble after the weekend to begin their preparations for the Australia clash on Sunday 8 November.

title: Novak Djokovic’s chances at the Swiss Indoors have just increased after major upset
article_text:
Novak Djokovic has two more chances to stake his claim for an ATP Finals position before the year-end tournament in November.

Djokovic is set to play the Swiss Indoors and the Paris Masters to try and gain enough ranking points to finish in the top nine of the ATP Tour race to Turin.

The Serbian currently sits at 11th in the ATP Race, but he still has a very good chance of qualifying for the event with deep runs at both tournaments.

He will begin his Swiss Indoors campaign with a first round match against Ugo Humbert in Basel, but results have already gone his way at the tournament.

He was set to play Casper Ruud in the quarterfinals of the ATP 500 tournament, if he made it that far, but the Norwegian is already out of the competition.

He was stunned in three sets by Nuno Borges, who beat the ninth seed 1-6, 6-3, 6-4 to earn his place in the last eight of the event.

That means that Djokovic can now reach the semifinals of the Swiss Indoors without playing a single seeded player.

However, he still has a long way to go before he makes it to the final four, with two victories to achieve at the tournament.

Humbert will provide a very difficult test for the 24-time Grand Slam champion and Jan-Lennard Struff already awaits in the second round of the tournament.

Nevertheless, Djokovic will be delighted with the players in his way as none of them are currently ranked inside the top 30 of the ATP Tour rankings.

In fact, Humbert, his first round opponent, is currently the highest ranked player he will have to play until the semifinalist.

The Frenchman is ranked world No 38 currently, which is 27 places below Djokovic’s current ranking.

From the semifinals is when things will get very tough for Djokovic, if he manages to reach the final four of the ATP 500 tournament.

Either Ben Shelton or Jiri Lehecka are his most likely semifinal opponent, although neither man has been able to defeat the Serbian in their careet yet.

Shelton lost his only match to Djokovic at the US Open in 2023, while Lehecka has lost both of his matches against the Serbian, at the United Cup in 2024 and the Australian Open in 2025.

Djokovic is looking to win the Swiss Indoors for just the second time in his career, after he won the tournament in 2009, beating Roger Federer in the final to win the ATP 500 tournament. Should he win the tournament, he will level Federer’s record of 103 ATP career titles.

title: Springboks star gone with immediate effect after investigation into conduct
article_text:
Bongi Mbonambi has left the Sharks with immediate effect and will return to the Stormers in a surprise move following an investigation into his conduct.

The Springboks hooker is set to return to Cape Town ahead of this weekend’s United Rugby Championship (URC) action, with Stormers director of rugby John Dobson confirming the transfer.

The 35-year-old, who helped South Africa win the Rugby World Cup in 2019 and 2023, is expected to report for duty on Wednesday.

Mbonambi spent six seasons with the Stormers before joining the Sharks in 2021, but his future in Durban had been uncertain for several weeks following allegations of misconduct during a pre-season team-building trip.

According to reports in South Africa, the hooker was at the centre of an internal disciplinary process after allegedly breaching team protocols during a camp at Bayala Private Safari Lodges.

Afrikaans newspaper Rapport reported that players had been given permission to socialise on the Tuesday evening but were expected to follow instructions from head coach JP Pietersen regarding their return to training.

Mbonambi was alleged to have breached those instructions. The Sharks subsequently left him out of training and matchday squads, despite reports that he was fit to play.

Another senior Springbok, Trevor Nyakane, was also reportedly involved in a breach of protocols, although Rapport suggested he could avoid more serious punishment because he was not present at the meeting in which Pietersen outlined the team's expectations.

Pietersen declined to discuss Mbonambi's absence when questioned at a Sharks media conference on October 8.

“Bongi is obviously not up for selection. There’s no comment about Bongi,” he said.

Mbonambi's departure brings an end to his latest spell with the Sharks, with the veteran hooker now returning to familiar surroundings at the Stormers.

He has won 82 caps for South Africa and remains one of the country's most experienced players, having played a prominent role in their back-to-back World Cup triumphs.

His return to Cape Town offers a fresh start after a difficult period in Durban, and boosts his chances of returning to the Springboks set-up ahead of next year's World Cup.

title: Ahn Se-young may skip Korea Open after 50-match win streak amid injury concerns
article_text:
World No. 1 Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) might not actually be seen in Korea.

Ahn Se-young returned home through Incheon International Airport on the morning of the 27th. Ahn Se-young recently asserted her dominance in women's singles by winning consecutive titles at the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Denmark Open and France Open. Riding a 50-match winning streak, Ahn Se-young recorded her 10th victory of the season.

Her results this year are overwhelming. Ahn Se-young went 66-1 in 67 matches played in 2026, achieving a 98.5% winning percentage. Since losing to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March, she has continued a 50-match winning streak.

Her strength shone even on the European tour. In the Denmark Open final she held off a fierce challenge from Yamaguchi, and at the France Open she lost the first game to Sindhu but changed her match strategy to complete a come-from-behind victory.

Meeting reporters after returning home, Ahn Se-young said she had worried because her physical condition had not improved as much as expected, but added that she was very happy to finish with good results.

Despite consecutive wins, there was no time to fully enjoy the joy. Ahn Se-young said winning matches is very good and makes her happy, but she tries to forget about it after a day passes, adding that with the next match and tournament coming up she has little time to celebrate. She said it is good for preparing anew toward the next goal, but it is a bit regrettable that she cannot deeply feel the afterglow of winning.

She also explained the crown ceremony she performed immediately after the France Open final. After beating Sindhu, Ahn Se-young made a crown shape with both hands and placed it above her head, saying she performed the ceremony because the season's schedule was nearly finished and she wanted to celebrate herself.

Behind the flashy results, there are concerns about injuries. Ahn Se-young won the women's singles gold medal at the 2026 Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games last month, achieving the sport's first back-to-back Asian Games titles. After about a week of regrouping, she immediately embarked on the European tour and went on to win two consecutive tournaments.

The problem is that the nonstop schedule has taken a toll on her body. In the Denmark Open final she felt pain in the area of her right Achilles tendon during the final third game and also appeared to twist her foot. Regarding the situation at the time, Ahn Se-young added that the court at the Denmark Open was very slippery although she had been fine in France, and that she had discomfort in her Achilles tendon but did not think she was injured, so she kept playing.

Ultimately, Ahn Se-young has not yet decided whether she will participate in the Korea Open held on home soil. Ahn Se-young delayed the answer, saying she will rest first and then decide.

title: World Rugby delivering Global Sport for Good in partnership with the International Olympic Committee
article_text:
Since 2024, the Global Sport for Good Initiative has brought together four international sports federations – World Rugby, FIBA (Basketball), World Athletics and BWF (Badminton) – and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to develop and harness the role that sport participation has in enhancing wellbeing, inclusion and community development globally.

The Global Sport for Good Initiative aims to strengthen programmes across World Rugby and partner international federations, broaden participation in sport, and increase its contribution to resilient communities, health and wellbeing, education and inclusion. To achieve these outcomes, World Rugby, the IOC and partner federations are placing community players’ needs at the centre of sport delivery, embedding this approach in grassroots coach education and workforce development, and improving how they measure and demonstrate impact.

1. Strengthening the delivery of sports by supporting coaches and community practitioners to put participant needs at the centre of how sport is delivered, while building their skills to increase access to sport, and create positive societal change.

2. World Rugby, sharing, exchanging and evidencing impact by unions and regions around the globe with the tools and knowledge to better measure, improve and understand the outcomes of their community training and education programmes, with a focus on health and wellbeing, inclusion, education and community development.

3. Strengthen peer learning and knowledge sharing between the four international federations, unions, regions and partners to strengthen delivery of community sport programmes and create opportunities to extend the reach and impact of sport, including through collaboration with broader stakeholders and partners.

1. Societal impact is systematically strengthened within the strategies, programmes, and operations of World Rugby, member regions and member unions, contributing to more sustainable, inclusive, and impactful sport systems.

2. World Rugby, member regions and unions increase the design and delivery of inclusive sport opportunities, resulting in greater participation and enhanced development of resilience, life skills, and other positive outcomes among participants.

3. Coaches, educators, and sport practitioners across World Rugby systems are strengthened and recognised as key actors in delivering positive societal outcomes through sport.

4. World Rugby, regions and our member unions increasingly position and leverage sport as a tool for societal impact, advancing health, education, inclusion, and broader development outcomes through their policies, programmes, and partnerships.

Since its launch in 2024, the initiative has supported capacity building of key groups across the four IFs and their networks, including Development Commissions at World Athletics, Regional and Union Training Managers at World Rugby, Local Facilitators at FIBA Foundation, and Community Educators at BWF. 500+ coaches, educators and 148 National Federations across 122 countries and 5 continents have been engaged globally. Each IF has also developed a Theory of Change to align its work with shared outcomes and indicators, supported by a common Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) approach.

Guided by a vision of a future where sport is part of everyday life for more people Global Sport for Good is part of the Olympic movement’s aim to positively transform lives through sport.

World Rugby Head of Education, Laws and Compliance Jock Peggie spoke of his pride in the project and the role of our Regional Training Managers “Putting young people at the heart of coaching both in how we deliver, ensuring we are supporting them to play an active role in wider society is a founding principle of rugby union and a key aim of World Rugby.

“I’m proud of how our Regional Training Managers, delivering all around the globe are empowering regions and unions to look closely at the way we bring young people into our sport and help coaches to encourage those young people to lead active lives wherever they grow up.”

title: Dyn COO Wontorra chosen to lead Frauen-Bundesliga into new era
article_text:
Marcel Wontorra will leave his role as chief operating officer of German sports streaming platform Dyn Media to become the new managing director of the Frauen-Bundesliga, the top-flight domestic women’s soccer league.

The Frauen-Bundesliga board and the club representatives involved in the selection process unanimously voted for Wontorra to lead the league’s newly established organizing body. The process was overseen by advisory firm Egon Zehnder.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Last month, the national DFB governing body confirmed plans to spin off the Frauen-Bundesliga into an independent body, bringing it in line with the men’s Bundesliga operationally.

Frauen-Bundesliga FBL e.V., a representative body established in December encompassing the 14 member clubs, acquired the rights to run the new organization on a seven-year lease from the DFB, which will remain the parent company.

A new registered limited company will be set up to manage commercial and logistical operations and future development.

This decision, which was approved unanimously by DFB delegates, will take effect on July 1, 2027. Wontorra will lead the new body, although his official start date is yet to be determined.

Katharina Kiel, president of FBL e.V., said: “With Marcel Wontorra, we are gaining a proven sports and media manager who combines strategic clarity, commercial expertise, and strong implementation skills.

“He is a pragmatic doer who wins over diverse stakeholders to common goals, thinks entrepreneurially, and tackles operational challenges. This combination is particularly valuable for FBL in its current development phase.”

Wontorra joined Dyn in 2022 and was involved from the beginning of the sports streaming platform's development. As COO, his responsibilities include editorial content, sports rights, business intelligence, finance, and human resources.

He played a key role in building the media platform and developing partnerships with sports leagues and associations. Previously, he worked for several years at Axel Springer, the German publishing giant.

On his new role, Wontorra said: “The Frauen-Bundesliga has great potential to continue growing, both on and off the field, in the coming years.

“Together with the clubs, we want to expand the league’s media and digital reach and increase its appeal for fans, players, and media and sponsoring partners. The board has created excellent conditions for this.”

The spin-off immediately necessitated a new Frauen-Bundesliga domestic media rights tender, which was launched in late September.

Rights to the competition are currently split across four broadcasters: streaming service DAZN, Magenta Sport (owned by T-Mobile), and public service networks ARD and ZDF.

title: Injury-hit Stormers confirm capture of double world champion Mbonambi
article_text:
Double World Cup winner Bongi Mbonambi has returned to the Stormers on a one-year deal.

The Springbok hooker, who made 74 appearances in his first spell with the club between 2015 and 2021, moves to Cape Town from the Sharks, after his contract there was terminated with the agreement of both parties following a disciplinary dispute.

Mbonambi is available for selection with immediate effect and is set to feature in the United Rugby Championship encounter with Ulster at DHL Stadium on Saturday.

With hookers André-Hugo Venter, Deon Fourie, Lukhanyo Vokozela, Almero Keizer and Luca Bakkes all injured and JJ Kotzé currently serving a suspension, the Stormers have turned to Mbonambi to help them through a difficult period.

“We all know the quality that Bongi brings and it is fantastic that we were able to arrange this deal at such short notice. We are grateful to both Bongi and the Sharks for helping to make this happen,” said Director of Rugby John Dobson

“Bongi became a Springbok while playing for us and has proven himself among the best in the world in the middle of the front row.

“We have been hit hard with both injuries and suspension to our hookers, so we are delighted to welcome Bongi back to the fold,” he said.

Mbonambi said that he is looking forward to making an impact for the DHL Stormers again.

“I spent many incredible years playing for the DHL Stormers, so to be back in Cape Town surrounded by so many people I know and respect is fantastic.

“This club is in a great space and I want to do all I can to contribute to the cause,” he said.

title: Shock coach departure prompts 52-word statement from URC club
article_text:
High-flying United Rugby Championship outfit Glasgow Warriors have confirmed that assistant coach Roddy Grant has left the club with immediate effect, following the outcome of an internal process.

The former Edinburgh flanker and Scotland 7s player worked with Glasgow’s forwards, with a specific remit for breakdown and contact work. Glasgow say he will not be replaced this season, with the existing coaching structure remaining the same.

Currently, Nigel Carolan (attack) and Scott Forrest (defence) serve under head coach Franco Smith, with support from academy coaches Shade Munro and former Scotland fly-half Duncan Weir.

Glasgow, who are second in the URC table, did not disclose any further details about the nature of Grant’s departure from Scotstoun, his place of work since the summer of 2025.

Prior to joining Glasgow, the 39-year-old had a brief spell as assistant to Richard Cockerill with the Georgia national team.

Cockerill and Grant knew each other from their time together at Edinburgh, where Grant was forwards coach in 2017 when the ex-England hooker took charge of the team.

Botswana-born Grant has been coaching since 2015, having initially developed his craft working with London Scottish and the Scottish Rugby Academy.

A five-year spell at Ulster, which followed his stint at Edinburgh, is the longest he has been at one club.

A statement from Glasgow read: “Glasgow Warriors can confirm that Roddy Grant has left the club following the conclusion of an internal process.

“Grant will not be replaced for the remainder of the 2026/27 season, the club will continue with its existing coaching structure.

“For reasons of confidentiality, the club will not be providing any further comment.”

title: Melbourne Storm Announce adidas as Official Apparel Partner
article_text:
Melbourne Storm has finalised a multi-year commercial agreement naming global sportswear brand adidas as the club’s Official Apparel Partner.

The partnership encompasses technical kit supply across the premier National Rugby League (NRL) squad, alongside the club’s elite male and female pathways and academy programs.

The official on-field debut of the three-stripes kit will take place during the opening round of the 2027 NRL season, when Craig Bellamy’s side travels to Las Vegas for the club’s inaugural regular-season fixture on U.S. soil. The partnership launch was accompanied by a custom brand film featuring key first-grade players Trent Loiero, Harry Grant, Cameron Munster, Sua Fa’alogo, and Jahrome Hughes alongside club legends Robbie Kearns, Ryan Hoffman, and head coach Craig Bellamy.

Melbourne Storm chief commercial and customer officer, Tayah Bot, emphasised the value of joining adidas’ international roster of high-performance sporting partners.

“Melbourne Storm has always prided itself on being a Club built different, and adidas is a partner that shares our ambition, our values and commitment to excellence.”

“We’re incredibly proud to welcome adidas as our Official Apparel Partner and to join forces with one of the world’s most iconic sporting brands.

“We can’t wait to see our new adidas playing kits, training wear and lifestyle apparel across our Melbourne Storm NRL and Pathway programs and throughout our community.

“There’s no better way to launch our partnership than debuting our new NRL jersey on the world stage in Las Vegas to kick-off our 2027 season,” Bot said.

Highligting the cultural alignment between the two organisations, GM of adidas Pacific, Rachel Howard, said: “Melbourne Storm has built a strong and distinctive identity through its commitment to discipline, resilience and performance, and those qualities are what make this partnership such a natural fit for adidas.”

“We’re excited to bring the Three Stripes to Melbourne Storm, and work alongside the Club’s players, members and fans as we look ahead to the 2027 season and beyond,” Howard said.

adidas Pacific operates as a subsidiary of adidas AG, located in Herzogenaurach, Germany, which reported global revenues of €24.8 billion for the 2025 financial year.

title: Lakers introduce new sponsorship opportunity with Just Ingredients logo on press conference microphones
article_text:
LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Lakers are taking sports sponsorships to a new level, introducing a unique advertising opportunity that puts a corporate partner front and center whenever their head coach and players address the media.

The Lakers announced Tuesday that Just Ingredients, a health and wellness company, has become the team's official electrolyte partner. But perhaps the most intriguing aspect of the partnership isn't what players will be drinking on the sidelines. It's what will be displayed on the microphones they speak into during press conferences.

The Just Ingredients logo will appear on the microphone flags in the Lakers' press conference room, where head coach JJ Redick speaks before and after games and players such as Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler address reporters following games.

While corporate sponsorships have long been a fixture of professional sports, with company logos appearing on everything from jerseys and courts to interview backdrops, the Lakers are introducing a different way to generate exposure for their partners.

Microphone flags, the small boxes surrounding microphones that typically display television network or media outlet logos, are familiar sights at press conferences. Using them to promote a team sponsor rather than a broadcaster represents an unusual approach to sports marketing.

The placement ensures that the Just Ingredients logo will be prominently displayed in photos, television broadcasts, social media clips and other video content whenever Lakers players and the head coach speak at the podium.

Unlike traditional advertising that relies on fans noticing a logo in the background, the microphone flag places the sponsor directly beneath the face of the person speaking, making it difficult to miss in close-up shots that often circulate widely following games.

The approach could provide a new sponsorship opportunity for professional sports franchises looking to maximize the commercial value of their media operations, particularly as press conference clips featuring star athletes generate millions of views across digital platforms.

The Lakers, one of the NBA's most recognizable franchises, offer an especially valuable platform with Doncic, Reaves and Redick regularly generating national headlines and significant social media engagement.

“We’re excited to welcome Just Ingredients to the Lakers organization and look forward to bringing the brand’s electrolyte products to players and fans throughout the season,” said Yao Williams, the Lakers' vice president of global partnerships.

Beyond the microphone placement, the agreement will make Just Ingredients electrolyte products available to Lakers players at the team's UCLA Health Training Center and in their game-day environment.

The company also plans to introduce a co-branded canned electrolyte beverage later this season featuring the Lakers' signature purple and gold colors.

Karalynne Call, founder and CEO of Just Ingredients, said the partnership provides an opportunity to reach a new generation of consumers through one of the world's most recognizable basketball teams.

"I've always believed that if we want to change the next generation, we have to show them what's possible," Call said. "Athletes do that better than anyone, and the Lakers inspire millions of young fans every season. Having our electrolytes on their sideline for local games is a meaningful step toward making real ingredients the standard for every athlete, every family, and every body."

Just Ingredients markets itself as a wellness and lifestyle company focused on ingredient transparency and products formulated without unnecessary additives.

For the Lakers, the agreement reflects the growing creativity of professional sports sponsorships, where teams are increasingly looking beyond traditional advertising inventory to create new opportunities for corporate partners.

And while the electrolyte products will be available to players behind the scenes, the company's most visible presence could come when Redick steps to the podium after a game or Doncic sits down to discuss another memorable performance.

For a franchise whose press conferences regularly become national news, even the microphone has become valuable advertising space.

title: Rugby legend Shane Williams comes out of retirement at 49 for special match
article_text:
Shane Williams will join a number of former players who are pulling on their boots once more for a charity match in Cardiff on Friday.

Wales' all-time top try-scorer will run out at the Arms Park on Friday night in this year's Match for Mental Health - a charity fixture raising funds for mental health charities LooseHeadz and Tough Enough to Care. The 49-year-old, who retired from the game in 2015, will line up alongside the likes of Marc Breeze, Olly Robinson, Sam Cross and Chris Czekaj.

Former Wales internationals Josh Navidi and Scott Andrews will also be involved as coaches.

This is the second year of the charity match, following the first game last year.

“The last charity rugby match I played was against Tough Enough To Care," said Williams about donning his boots once more. “I was apprehensive about playing contact rugby again, but once we started running around, laughing and joking, it all came back.

“You make a tackle, somebody tackles you and your mate picks you up off the floor. It takes you back — whether that is to a Grand Slam, a World Cup semi-final or a game you played at school.

“It reminded me how much I love rugby and the people around it. As long as my body can cope, I would like to keep doing things like this.

“My brother-in-law is playing in the same team on Friday, and I have not played alongside him for about seven years. That will be special.

“There is the catching up before and after, the interaction with supporters and, most importantly, raising awareness for these charities.

“I still get nervous and excited, which takes me back to those big games. I cannot wait.”

Speaking about what stands out about both charities, Williams added: “The openness and honesty.

“People look at rugby players as these big, physical people who run over opponents and make huge tackles. These charities help show that mental health affects people regardless of how strong they look.

“Rugby is a game for all shapes and sizes. Whether you are the smallest scrum-half or a huge prop, you can relate to somebody on the field.

“If a big, physical rugby player can speak openly about struggling, it helps show that anybody can.

“Both charities have brilliant people involved, including former players and internationals who understand the challenges of sport, retirement and feeling alone.

“They help create those conversations. On Friday, that might start with catching up, having a laugh and talking to somebody you have not seen for years.

“Before you know it, you might be organising a golf trip with 10 former teammates. That reconnection is part of what it is about.”

Following Friday's match, Williams will be back to his punditry duties - alongside his work as head of rugby academy at Ysgol Dyffryn Aman.

And he is hopeful Steve Tandy's side will enjoy a solid Nations Championship campaign next month.

“I certainly hope we are ready to beat Japan, and I think we are," he said.

“There is some positivity in Welsh rugby. The regions are doing reasonably well, and hopefully that feeds into the national team.

“The Ospreys had a good bonus-point win at St Helen’s. The Dragons have shown encouraging signs under Filo Tiatia, Cardiff are doing well and the Scarlets are playing some good rugby.

“Steve Tandy is well respected and has put together a decent squad.

“Do I see Wales beating the All Blacks? Probably not. But Japan and Australia should be games they target, particularly at home.

“I hope the support is there and we can get some positivity back around the Welsh jersey. I am backing the boys.”

Shane Williams was speaking on behalf of LooseHeadz and Tough Enough to Care ahead of this Friday’s Match for Mental Health at Cardiff Arms Park, kicking off at 7.30pm.

Adult tickets cost £10, with free admission for children under 10. Tickets are available through Cardiff Rugby’s ticketing website.

Further information is available on the LooseHeadz event page.

Glasgow Warriors confirm Roddy Grant departure after 'internal process'
article_text:
Glasgow Warriors have confirmed that assistant coach Roddy Grant has left the club following the conclusion of an "internal process".

The club announced Grant’s departure in a brief statement, with his exit taking immediate effect.

The Warriors have also confirmed they will not appoint a replacement for the remainder of the 2026/27 campaign.

Instead, the Scotstoun side will continue with their existing coaching structure, with Nigel Carolan as attack coach and Scott Forrest as defence coach alongside Franco Smith, plus academy coaches Shade Munro and Duncan Weir, for the rest of the season.

Glasgow did not disclose any details regarding the internal process which preceded Grant’s departure.

A club statement read: “Glasgow Warriors can confirm that Roddy Grant has left the club following the conclusion of an internal process.

“Grant will not be replaced for the remainder of the 2026/27 season, the club will continue with its existing coaching structure.

“For reasons of confidentiality, the club will not be providing any further comment.”

Grant joined Glasgow in June 2025 following a stint on the coaching staff of the Georgian national team under Richard Cockerill, who was head coach at the time.

He had previously spent five years as Ulster’s forwards coach and, prior to that, had been on the coaching staff at Edinburgh, the club for which he played for six seasons.

Former back-row forward Grant played 138 times for Edinburgh, and was captain of the club, while he also represented Scotland at the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

title: Alex Eala +2 to milestone position in WTA Rankings as she reaches Pan Pacific Open quarter-finals
article_text:
Alex Eala progressed to the quarter-finals of the 2026 Pan Pacific Open after a three-set comeback victory against Talia Gibson.

The Filipina star downed world No 38 Gibson 4-6, 6-2, 6-0 in the second round at the WTA 500 tournament in Tokyo on Wednesday.

Eala lost the opening set after she was broken at 3-4 and 4-5, but she did not lose serve again thereafter and broke her 22-year-old Australian opponent twice in the second set and three times in the third to complete a dominant turnaround.

The 21-year-old started the week as the world No 19 — one place below her career-high ranking position of 18th.

After reaching the last eight at the Pan Pacific Open, Eala has moved onto 2,289 ranking points.

According to the Live WTA Rankings on live-tennis.eu, Eala is back up to her peak position of 18th.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Victoria Mboko, who has been sidelined since June due to a knee injury, has fallen from 15th to 20th in the Live Rankings as she is dropping 250 points this week.

Eala is currently 26 points behind Naomi Osaka in 17th place, 74 points adrift of Amanda Anisimova in 16th, and 97 points below 15th-placed Sorana Cirstea.

Eala dismantled 17-year-old British wildcard Mika Stojsavljevic 6-1, 6-2 in the opening round in Tokyo on Monday.

Following her first round win, Eala said: “I think it was super important today to be focused on every single point. Playing against Mika for the first time was a great experience and I am sure we will meet many, many more times.

“I think she has a really good level and I’ll see her many more times on Tour. I think it was super important to be focused, especially in the first round, and try to keep the intensity up.”

In her next match, Eala will face world No 13 Diana Shnaider in the quarter-finals at the Pan Pacific Open.

It will be a rematch of the pair’s second round encounter at the Ningbo Open last week, which Shnaider won 7-5, 6-4.

title: Smashing Stats: HYLO Open 2026
article_text:
Stefani and Gabriela Stoeva after winning their second HYLO Open, then known as SaarLorLux Open, in 2020.

A strong field of world class shuttlers conclude the European leg of the HSBC BWF World Tour at the Super 500 HYLO Open 2026.

As the tournament celebrates its 39th edition, here are some stats to look out for.

Germany have not won a title since mixed pair Michael Fuchs/Birgit Michels triumphed in 2013.

Marvin Seidel/Nguyen Thuc Phuong, coming off a strong showing at the French Open, are their only seeded hope this year, at No.8.

Denmark are the nation with most number of titles (40).

Across the last two editions, the Danes have won four.

Two of those came in women’s singles and mixed doubles. Another victory in either discipline would make Denmark the first country in a decade to win the same event thrice in a row.

China were the last to achieve the feat, in women’s doubles in 2016.

Denmark have not won men’s singles after Rasmus Gemke in 2017. Top seed Anders Antonsen will lead their bid to end that drought.

Top-seeded world champions Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue could become France’s first-ever mixed doubles winners at the tournament.

Indonesia have yet to produce a winning women’s combo. They look to break that duck with three seeded combos: Rachel Allessya Rose/Febi Setianingrum (2), Febriana Dwipuji Kusuma/Meilysa Trias Puspitasari (3) and Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti (5).

Pairs representing six different flags have taken the women’s doubles crown since 2020.

Fourth seeds Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva could become the most decorated women’s tandem of this century with a third HYLO Open success.

Men’s doubles has gone the longest without back-to-back winners, with Mathias Boe/Carsten Mogensen the last pair to do so in consecutive editions (2008).

Jonatan Christie, Chiu Hsiang Chieh/Wang Chi Lin and Margot Lambert/Camille Pognante are the returning defending champions.

Standout Stat: Should Seidel/Nguyen triumph, Germany, currently on 39.5 titles, will overtake Denmark as the most successful nation in tournament history.

title: Carlos Alcaraz And Alexander Zverev Win Vienna Openers
LIV Golf captain drops clue about his future plans after sharing hospital bed picture
article_text:
Martin Kaymer has confirmed he has gone under the knife for his second operation in the space of two months.

The big German, who memorably sank a six-foot putt at Medinah Country Club to complete a miracle comeback for Europe at the 2012 Ryder Cup, revealed on 18 September that he had shoulder surgery after a "challenging year".

Now he has undergone a procedure on his elbow.

Kaymer told his followers on Instagram that the latest operation should not affect his recovery from shoulder surgery.

"Hopefully, that’s the last of the repairs for a while," the LIV Golf recruit said.

Kaymer added: "Looking forward to starting 2027 fully recovered and ready to play wherever it might be!"

The 41-year-old was referring to the fact LIV Golf's future remains far from certain.

Kaymer joined LIV Golf for its inaugural season in 2022, taking on the captaincy of Cleeks GC.

The two-time major winner has struggled to recapture his best form in recent years, and his 2026 campaign was another difficult one.

He finished no higher than a tie for 24th in the individual standings at a LIV event this season, at Andalucia in June, while his best result was a tie for 24th.

He ended the season ranked 53rd in the league's individual standings, having missed the Adelaide event with the aforementioned elbow injury.

His latest operations will now give him the chance to focus on his recovery ahead of next season, although it remains unclear whether he will be playing on LIV Golf in 2027.

The circuit has faced major uncertainty following the decision of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund to end its financial backing after the 2026 season.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September and are working through a court-supervised process to emerge from the ashes.

London-based credit firm, BC Partners, have agreed to provide $300m in funding but needs a "critical mass" of LIV players to commit to its new era.

Sources have told GolfMagic they are extremely confident of launching LIV 2.0 in 2027, despite a number of high-profile players to confirm they are leaving.

Kaymer's former Ryder Cup teammates, Ian Poulter and Graeme McDowell. are among those to have bolted.

Their decisions to walk away after four years with LIV brought the number of departures to 13.

Jon Rahm was the highest-profile player to leave LIV after deeming the terms to remain as "unacceptable".

Adrian Meronk, David Puig, Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell II, Thomas Piters, Lous Oosthuizen, Branden Grace, Lucas Herbert and Tyrrell Hatton have also quit.

The Financial Times reported last week that LIV enough golfers had committed to keep hopes of a new league alive.

It is not clear if Kaymer was among the group of 15 players.

Speaking to to Today's Golfer in July, Kaymer appeared to indicate he would prefer to stick with LIV.

"Hopefully, I think there's a lot of interest [from new investors] and it's looking good," he said.

"But we've all been there. If the signature is not there, then it doesn't mean anything," added the German.

"If those investors decide to pull out then we don't play next year on LIV Golf.

"And if they decide to do it, then we have a chance."

title: Jewel in Aussie golf crown gets even bigger as superstar confirmed
article_text:
Min Woo Lee has officially confirmed he will compete for the Stonehaven Cup at the Australian Open from December 3-6.

The announcement comes after the Aussie star committed to playing at the Australian PGA Championship from November 26-29, setting up a huge fortnight of golf on home soil.

Lee, who is ranked 31st in the world, will join some of golf’s biggest names at Kingston Heath, including Rory McIlroy, Sahith Theegala and Ryan Fox.

Speaking after confirming his Australian Open appearance, Lee admitted he was desperate to finally get his hands on the Stonehaven Cup after several near misses.

“The Australian Open is a big one for us Aussies, and winning the Stonehaven Cup is something every Australian golfer dreams about, especially on a Sandbelt course,” Lee said.

“I’ve come close a few times, so hopefully this can be the year I get it done. It’s definitely one of the tournaments I really want to win.”

Lee has twice finished third at the Australian Open, most recently in 2023 when he entered the final round tied for the lead before falling two shots short of a playoff.

That result came just a week after he claimed the Australian PGA Championship, narrowly missing the chance to complete the Australian double.

Despite enjoying a strong 2026 campaign, Lee is still searching for his first victory of the year and hopes that will come at Kingston Heath.

“The game’s been solid this year, with some great results. I’ve just been missing that win, so hopefully I can get hot at Kingston Heath and give myself a chance.”

Lee has recorded six top-10 finishes this season, including two runner-up results, while also finishing tied for fourth at the Tour Championship.

Golf Australia CEO James Sutherland said Lee’s return would be a major boost for the tournament, with the Aussie star expected to attract plenty of support from the home crowd.

“Min Woo is one of the most exciting players in world golf, and Australian fans love watching him play,” Sutherland said.

“He has had a really strong year and the game to make a huge impact at Kingston Heath.

“Min Woo always brings plenty of energy to an event, and with the quality of the field taking shape, we’re expecting a terrific week of golf at Kingston Heath.”

The Australian Open will be played at Kingston Heath Golf Club in Melbourne from December 3-6, following the Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club in Sydney from November 26-29.

Australian golf has received a major boost, with the PGA Tour, DP World Tour and Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia announcing an expanded partnership.

As part of the deal, the BMW Australian PGA Championship will remain a co-sanctioned Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia and DP World Tour event for another three years.

The agreement will help attract international talent to one of Australia’s biggest tournaments, while creating more opportunities for local golfers.

PGA of Australia Chair Ian Baker-Finch welcomed the deal, saying it would create more opportunities for Aussie golfers and strengthen the country’s biggest tournaments.

“Securing the BMW Australian PGA Championship as a co-sanctioned event for a further three years alongside the Australian Open is another important part of that,” Baker-Finch said.

“Our major tournaments provide an opportunity for our players to compete against world-class fields on home soil and showcase professional golf in this country to audiences at home around the world.”

PGA of Australia CEO Gavin Kirkman pointed to Min Woo Lee as a prime example of how the partnership has helped Aussie golfers make their mark on the world stage.

Lee won the co-sanctioned Vic Open in 2020 before going on to claim the Scottish Open in 2021 and Australian PGA Championship in 2023.

Meanwhile, DP World Tour Chief Tournament and Operations Officer Ben Cowen reinforced the importance of the Australian PGA Championship to the tour’s international calendar.

“As we near our return down under in November, we are excited to again be opening our season with the BMW Australian PGA Championship,” Cowen said.

“This tournament is a key launchpad for the Race to Dubai, and we look forward to having it part of our global schedule for a further three years.”

title: HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final: Field, format and prize purse as players battle for DP World Tour promotion in Mallorca
article_text:
The HotelPlanner Tour season reaches its climax this week at the Grand Final, live on Sky Sports, with a past Ryder Cup player, previous tournament winners and ex-LIV golfers among those chasing promotion to the DP World Tour.

What is the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final and the Road to Mallorca Rankings?

This year's event marks the 31st time the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final has been played and will bring the curtain down on the DP World Tour feeder circuit's 28-event season.

- What golf is live on Sky Sports and when? Full TV listings

It will also conclude the HotelPlanner Tour's points competition, the Road to Mallorca Rankings, with the top-45 golfers in the standings set to tee up this week in hopes of securing a coveted DP World Tour card for next season.

James Morrison won the event in 2025, while JC Ritchie topped the Road to Mallorca Rankings.

Club de Golf Alcanada, situated on Mallorca's south-east coast, has hosted the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final for the past five years and is set to stage the 2026 showpiece once again.

At the end of the tournament, the top 15 players in the Road to Mallorca standings will be awarded a DP World Tour card for next season.

And we're set for a thrilling finale, with every player in the 45-man field able to earn promotion to the DP World Tour.

Four-thousand Road to Mallorca Rankings Points are up for grabs, with the winner of the Grand Final awarded 640 points. Second place will claim 440 points and third will secure 280 points.

American Alex Goff is the lowest-ranked player in the field on 447.30 points. Meanwhile, England's Matthew Southgate sits in the final DP World Tour qualifying spot. The pair are separated by 243.55 points, meaning Goff could jump into the top 15 with a win.

A £418,000 (€500,000) prize fund is also up for grabs.

Tapio Pulkkanen, enters the tournament fifth in the Road to Mallorca standings and is bidding to become the first player to have won the HotelPlanner Tour's order of merit twice, after he finished No 1 in 2017.

Current Road to Mallorca Rankings leader, Hamish Brown, will have his sights set on holding down the No 1 spot. Brown comes into the week in good form after winning the tour's penultimate event, the Hangzhou Open, on October 18.

Swedish golfer Christofer Blomstrand and Lars Van der Vight trail him in second, and third place and will both be keen to leapfrog Brown to snatch the No 1 spot.

Chris Wood, who featured at the 2016 Ryder Cup, is looking to return to the DP World Tour after losing his playing rights in 2022. Wood, who competed in the LIV Golf Promotions event in January, comes into the Grand Final ranked No 37.

Three other former LIV Golfers are in the field this week, including Frederik Kjetterup, who was relegated from LIV Golf in 2025 after signing for Cleeks GC in 2024.

Dominic Foos and John Catlin, who also featured in January's LIV Golf Promotions event, come into the event ranked 31st and 41st in the rankings.

Many European golfing stars have graduated to the DP World Tour following victories at the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final, including Thomas Bjorn in 1995, Edoardo Molinari in 2009 and Tommy Fleetwood in 2011.

More recently, Ryder Cup hopefuls Marco Penge and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen won at Club de Golf Alcanada in 2023 and 2024, respectively.

How can I watch the Grand Final on Sky Sports?

Fans can enjoy every moment of what is gearing up to be a nail-biting conclusion to the HotelPlanner Tour season with all the action live on Sky Sports.

The first three rounds are live on Sky Sports Golf from 11am, while Sunday's final-round coverage starts at 10.30am on the same channel.

title: Cobalt Digital goes for Gold SVG Europe sponsorship
article_text:
Cobalt Digital, a designer and manufacturer of signal processing products, and a founding partner in the openGear initiative, has renewed its Gold sponsorship of SVG Europe.

The company offers a range of ST 2110, IPMX, and SDI conversion, compression, processing, routing, control, and multiviewer technology for the production, broadcast television, and pro-AV environments.

It continues to expand its IPMX capabilities, with support for JPEG XS Temporal Differential Coding (JXS TDC), enabling IPMX-certified products to discover, establish and transport visually lossless, ultra-low latency JPEG XS media streams. JPEG-XS support is available across Cobalt’s ST 2110/IPMX-capable products, including Sapphire mini converters, Indigo gateways, Pacific encoders and decoders, Topaz processing platforms, Aria audio monitors and UltraBlue multiviewers.

Cobalt also recently debuted its blueCORE family of standalone signal processors, which deliver powerful, multi-function audio and video processing in a compact 1RU form factor, making it well suited for applications where space, power and operational simplicity matter. The platform supports both SDI and ST 2110/IPMX, allowing users to process signals within existing SDI environments while providing a direct path towards IP.

“SVG Europe helps Cobalt stay connected to the people, emerging trends and challenges shaping the future of sports broadcasting. Its high-level content keeps our team informed on issues specific to sports production, while its summits, regional forums and technical forums provide valuable opportunities to exchange ideas with industry peers and showcase our latest technologies,” said Suzana Brady, SVP of worldwide sales and marketing for Cobalt Digital. “Moving forward, our growing IPMX/ST 2110 ecosystem helps sports broadcasters transition to IP at their own pace while supporting hybrid SDI/IP workflows. We’re pleased to renew our sponsorship of SVG Europe and look forward to continuing to support the sports broadcast community.”

title: Chadwicks Gives Trade Supplier Front-of-Shirt Spotlight with Shelbourne
article_text:
Chadwicks has used its lead partnership with Shelbourne FC to give one of its trade customers a rare place at the centre of a major sporting sponsorship, handing Ashbourne-based A.S.K. Mechanical the front-of-shirt position across matches involving both the club’s men’s and women’s teams.

The mechanical contractor won the position through Chadwicks’ Jersey Swap competition, an initiative designed to turn one of the most visible assets within the Shelbourne partnership into a promotional platform for businesses from within the Chadwicks customer base.

A.S.K. Mechanical appeared on the front of the Shelbourne men’s jersey for the League of Ireland fixture against Sligo Rovers at Tolka Park on October 9.

A week later, on October 17, the branding moved to the women’s shirt as Shelbourne, fresh from winning the FAI Cup, faced Athlone Town.

Both games came during the closing stages of the respective domestic seasons and gave the company exposure to supporters in the ground, broadcast and digital audiences around the matches and the wider Shelbourne fan base.

The A.S.K. Mechanical team was also hosted in the recently developed hospitality area at Tolka Park, adding an experiential element to the prize.

Established in 2015 by Managing Director Alan Kelly, A.S.K. Mechanical provides domestic and commercial mechanical services, including heating systems, heat pumps, plumbing, ventilation, air conditioning, and mechanical fit-outs.

Its work spans healthcare, education, hospitality, commercial offices, warehousing, residential development and social housing.

“We were absolutely delighted to be selected for this fantastic opportunity from Chadwicks,” said Kelly.

“It was a really proud moment for the whole team to see the A.S.K. Mechanical logo on the front of both the Shelbourne men’s and women’s jerseys.”

“It was a great chance to showcase our business to a wider audience. Seeing our name on the pitch across both matchdays was a brilliant experience, and one we were thrilled to share with our colleagues, customers and families.”

Chadwicks has been developing its association with Shelbourne around a combination of traditional sponsorship visibility and engagement with the trade community which forms the core of its business.

“Congratulations to Alan and the team at A.S.K. Mechanical on winning the Chadwicks Jersey Swap competition,” said Tara Brennan, Marketing Director at Chadwicks Group.

“A.S.K. Mechanical has been a valued Chadwicks customer since the company was established in 2015, and we were delighted to afford them this opportunity to promote their business to a wide audience.”

The smartest sponsorship activations often take an asset a brand already owns and make it valuable to someone else.

Chadwicks could simply have retained its position on the Shelbourne shirt. Instead, it converted that visibility into something a trade customer could never normally access.

For A.S.K. Mechanical, the value lies in the scale and credibility that comes from seeing your company name on the front of a professional football shirt.

For Chadwicks, the bigger return is showing its wider customer community that its investment in sport can create opportunities for them, too.

That moves the partnership beyond awareness and toward relationship building, which, for a business rooted so heavily in the trade sector, is arguably the more valuable outcome.

Sport for Business explores how sport drives economic value, participation, inclusion and national identity, and how your story can be part of ours.

title: Radar Tyres signs sponsorship deal with Manny Pacquiao basketball league - Vietnam Investment Review
article_text:
SINGAPORE, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Radar Tyres today announced a multi-year partnership with the Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League (MPBL) as its Official Partner. The agreement was signed in General Santos City, Philippines, at the residence of MPBL founder and boxing legend Emmanuel "Manny" Pacquiao.

The deal is the homegrown brand's second major international sports partnership of 2026, following its appointment as Global Partner of Cricket South Africa (CSA), covering the Proteas Men's, Women's and U19 teams. Together, the two partnerships mark a significant step in Radar's journey from its roots in Singapore to a tyre brand on the world's sporting stages.

Radar Tyres is the flagship brand of Omni United, founded and headquartered in Singapore in 2003. The brand is now present in more than 80 countries, with a sports portfolio to match. Beyond CSA and the MPBL, Radar partners with Major League Baseball's Texas Rangers, sponsors Australian cricket legend Michael Clarke, and supports professional and amateur athletes in tennis and golf worldwide. At home, it supports up-and-coming golfers by partnering with the Singapore Golf Association (SGA).

Giving back has been part of Radar's DNA since its founding. That includes 15 years of support for the Breast Cancer Research Foundation, as well as backing athletes across tennis, golf, off-road racing and more. The brand believes great talent should never be held back by financial constraints.

That belief mirrors the MPBL's mission. Pacquiao founded the league in 2018 to give young Filipinos a positive path through sport. Today, it offers homegrown athletes a national platform to showcase their skills and build a livelihood. It brings high-level basketball to communities across the provinces, and every game is broadcast on free-to-air television.

The Philippines has been one of Radar's key Asia-Pacific markets for over 17 years. In a nation where basketball is a way of life, the MPBL connects Radar directly with fans, households and communities from north to south.

"Giving back to the community has always been in our DNA. It is who we are at Radar Tyres, and it is a commitment we have carried across every country we operate in," said GS Sareen, President and CEO, Omni United. "As a brand born and raised in Singapore, we are proud to see Radar stand alongside some of the most respected names in world sport, from the Proteas in South Africa to the MPBL in the Philippines. The Philippines holds a special place in our hearts. For over 17 years, Filipino drivers and dealers have welcomed our brand, and this partnership is our way of coming closer to them and the communities they call home. Across eight seasons, Manny Pacquiao and his team have built something truly remarkable - a grassroots league that uplifts young Filipinos through sport and gives rising talent the chance to be seen. Their mission reflects the very beliefs that guide us, and we are proud to stand alongside this exceptional league as it continues to grow."

"In basketball, just like in life, we go further when we move forward together. Through our partnership with Radar Tyres, we share a common mission – to support Filipino talent, strengthen our communities and give our athletes the opportunity to chase their dreams. Because when we invest in sports, we invest in the future of our Filipino youth," said Emmanuel "Manny" Pacquiao.

The partnership begins with the remainder of the MPBL Season 8 Playoffs and Finals and continues into Season 9. As Official Partner and exclusive tyre sponsor, Radar Tyres will have full category exclusivity, with brand visibility across broadcast, livestream, digital and on-court assets. With 28 teams expected to play around 400 games in the 2027 season, the partnership will carry the Singapore brand into homes across the Philippines.

Queensland Rugby Union and Buildcorp Finalise Three-Year Partnership Extension Through 2029
article_text:
The Queensland Rugby Union (QRU) and construction firm Buildcorp have announced a three-year extension of their commercial partnership, securing the agreement through 2029.

Buildcorp will remain the principal naming-rights partner of the Buildcorp Reds Academy, continuing a multi-year sponsorship that commenced in 2022 to support elite rugby union talent pathways across Queensland.

The Buildcorp Reds Academy operates a three-tier development structure catering to more than 70 high-performance male athletes aged 16 to 20.

The Academy serves as the primary player pipeline for the Queensland Reds Super Rugby Pacific squad, with athletes utilising the Ballymore-based BMS National Rugby Training Centre, a facility constructed and completed by Buildcorp in 2023.

Recent Academy graduates who have transitioned into professional and national representative squads include Queensland Reds players Treyvon Pritchard, Tom Robinson, Finn Mackay, and Australian U18 and U20 representative Taione Taka.

Commenting on the partnership extension, managing director and co-founder of Buildcorp, Tony Sukkar AM, said: “Each season, we see players stepping up to the Reds after foundations have been established in the Buildcorp Reds Academy.”

“It’s similar to how we operate with training, continual learning and establishing company values so it’s not a foreign thing when people step up a level.

“Social responsibility is another Buildcorp value and we see that in the community associations when young players come into the Academy.

“It’s been wonderful to be part of re-energising Ballymore and partnering in the construction of the world-class high-performance facility.

“It’s very satisfying to be involved in the QRU’s plans for long-term success.

“Some faces may change and the way a new coach plays the game but the strong culture at the Reds does not.

“That alignment with our own values at Buildcorp is very reassuring,” Sukkar said.

Emphasising the role Buildcorp plays in underpinning the organisation’s long-term high-performance vision, QRU CEO, David Hanham, added: “We are extremely grateful to be working with a like-minded business such as Buildcorp with long-term success so important to both of us.”

“The Sukkar family have a deep connection and care for rugby.

“With the people at Buildcorp, they have enriched rugby with their support over many years.

“Buildcorp’s support brings the Reds Academy to life. On a broader front, Buildcorp work with a number of QRU partners which shows the value of the commercial partner network we have built.

“We share excitement for what is ahead for Queensland rugby,” Hanham said.

The partnership extension expands Buildcorp’s 35-year sponsorship footprint across Australian rugby union, which has formerly included major investments in the Wallaroos national women’s team, Super Rugby Women’s, and ongoing club sponsorships with University of Queensland Rugby Club and Sydney University Football Club. The QRU alignment represents Buildcorp’s first direct investment into a state union pathway program.

title: Medvedev finds swift adjustment to overcome Merida, reach Vienna R2
article_text:
Daniil Medvedev arrived at the Erste Bank Open off the back of winning his fourth ATP Tour title of the year, but that did not mean a completely smooth start to his title bid in Vienna.

The third-seeded Medvedev recovered after a slow opening few games to down Daniel Merida 7-6(5), 6-1 and notch his Tour-leading 39th hard-court win of the year. Merida led 4-1 early at the Wiener Stadthalle, but last week’s Almaty champion Medvedev ultimately claimed an 88-minute triumph to extend his winning streak to five matches.

Medvedev will take on Cameron Norrie in the second round in Vienna, where he lifted the trophy in 2022. The 30-year-old will hope he has now completely adjusted to the conditions in the Austrian capital, after admitting he initially struggled with the contrast from Almaty.

“It’s just a matter of trying your best, because even if a court is slow or fast, I won on many courts, and even on different surfaces,” the former World No. 1 said. “I just needed to try my best and get used to it, because it’s not easy when on Sunday you are playing on one court, and Wednesday on another one. It’s a good win, I’m looking forward to the next one.”

With his first-round victory, Medvedev jumped above Flavio Cobolli into fifth in the PIF ATP Live Race To Turin. The 2020 Nitto ATP Finals champion, he is bidding to qualify for the prestigious season finale for the seventh time, having made six consecutive appearances from 2019 to 2024.

Tallon Griekspoor, who like Medvedev claimed an ATP 250 trophy on Sunday by winning Brussels, was also an early winner in Vienna on Wednesday. He edged Brandon Nakashima 6-1, 4-6, 7-6(2) to advance to face top seed Alexander Zverev.

Zverev leads Griekspoor 9-3 in the pair’s Lexus ATP Head2Head series, although the Dutchman won the pair’s most recent meeting in August in Montreal. Should Zverev win and reach the quarter-finals in Vienna, he will ensure he on Monday rises to No. 1 in the PIF ATP Rankings for the first time.

Sports Tech &ever Sponsors Korean, Laotian Football Clubs
article_text:
[OSEN=Seo Jeong-hwan reporter] Sports tech company &ever sponsors South Korea's global independent football club FC Abnill and Laos' professional football club Champasak HAGL Abnill FC, embarking on a global football collaboration connecting South Korea and Laos. The plan is to systematically record players' performance through support of professional match and filming equipment, and link player development with joint promotion.

This sponsorship will proceed by providing both clubs with professional match and filming equipment. The clubs plan to use this to systematically accumulate players' match footage and create an environment where performance analysis and growth management can be utilized.

In particular, match footage is significant as it objectively showcases individual players' skills and potential. While utilizing video records for player development, both clubs plan to actively produce promotional content highlighting players' performances. The plan is to inform domestic and international football officials and fans about the players' competitiveness and support them in gaining more opportunities on the global stage.

South Korea's FC Abnill and Laos' Champasak HAGL Abnill FC will also pursue joint promotion using match footage and club content. By sharing both clubs' match records and players' growth processes, they aim to enhance the clubs' competitiveness and expand the global football network connecting South Korea and Laos.

&ever CEO Kim Kang-min stated, "We find it meaningful to support football players in recording their performance through video and using it to showcase their potential to more people." He added, "We hope this collaboration will provide players with broader opportunities and lead to exchanges and development in football between the two countries."

He further added, "Moving forward, we will strive to support players' growth and club promotion activities based on our provision of match and filming equipment."

Bae Ji-sun, representative of both FC Abnill and Champasak HAGL Abnill FC, also expressed anticipation for this sponsorship.

Representative Bae stated, "This sponsorship is a great opportunity for both South Korean and Laotian clubs to record players' performance through professional filming equipment and joint promotion, increasing their exposure on the international stage." He added, "We hope to continue various collaborations and promotions to inform more football officials about the potential and competitiveness of professional and independent club players."

He continued, "We thank &ever for deciding on this collaboration and request continued interest and cooperation in the future."

This collaboration is notable as it goes beyond simple equipment support, connecting player development, content production, and joint club promotion based on match footage records. The aim is to establish a foundation for players continuing challenges across various countries and stages to record their performance and showcase their potential.

FC Abnill and Champasak HAGL Abnill FC plan to strengthen their player development environments through this sponsorship and build a sustainable global football collaboration model by sharing experiences and content between the two clubs. / jasonseo34@osen.co.kr
